speedrun: Inspect the repository layout, current status, and available build commands.
Read README, command documentation, configuration documentation, and output-format documentation.
Inspect git history for the original compiler, configuration migrations, reverted inheritance work, and compatibility-policy commits.
Run the command's help output and identify its input, configuration, and output paths.
Locate parser, configuration, compiler, dependency-resolution, registry, diagnostic, and serialization code.
Inspect generated fixtures and representative valid, malformed, inherited, cyclic, and compatibility-sensitive contracts.
Run the compiler on the supplied corpus, capturing stderr, exit status, output files, counts, and hashes.
Compare the generated registry and diagnostics with existing fixtures or documented expected behavior.
Inspect the wirecheck documentation and probe its request and response behavior on representative schemas.
Run focused differential tests with reordered files and JSON keys to expose nondeterminism.
Trace configuration loading to identify omitted-versus-explicit false or empty values and precedence rules.
Trace dependency scheduling and inheritance merging, including how errors propagate to descendants.
Trace helper failures and determine whether ambiguous or failed classifications are currently accepted.
Implement presence-aware configuration parsing and documented default and precedence semantics.
Implement complete dependency-graph construction and validation before compilation, including missing parents, cycles, and duplicate handling.
Implement transitive inheritance resolution with local-over-inherited policy precedence, aliases, exceptions, fields, and effective metadata.
Make every wirecheck failure or ambiguous result a deterministic contract rejection without aborting unrelated contracts.
Sort contracts, fields, aliases, diagnostics, and summary collections at every externally visible serialization boundary.
Stage registry, diagnostics, and summary outputs in temporary files and atomically rename them only after successful compilation.
Run gofmt, go vet or package tests, and rebuild the command.
Run the supplied corpus and inspect all outputs and diagnostics.
Generate or run reordered and repeated corpus cases, comparing byte-identical outputs.
Run generated deep graphs with missing parents, cycles, duplicate aliases, and inherited policy overrides.
Run malformed-document and rare wirecheck cases, checking recovery and deterministic rejection behavior.
Inject a late compilation or helper failure and verify prior outputs remain unchanged and no temporary artifacts remain.
Run the command twice on unchanged inputs and compare hashes, filesystem state, and summary contents.
Review the diff to ensure the CLI, configuration format, fixtures, and unrelated historical outputs were not changed.
invalid_failure_risks: The duplicate-contract and duplicate-alias semantics are not explicitly stated; tests could require a behavior that is absent from the documented configuration or repository history.
The requested helper-failure tests require a documented way to inject or induce wirecheck failures; without one, those tests may depend on unavailable platform behavior or undocumented helper cases.
The exact atomic-output contract for the summary file and pre-existing stale outputs after a failed run is not fully specified.
Generated corpus tests may become flaky if they depend on random generation without fixed seeds or if filesystem replacement and concurrency behavior are not controlled.
The requirement to preserve every valid contract is potentially inconsistent with duplicate names unless the registry's collision policy is explicitly defined.
review.reasons: The task defines a concrete end state and exercises independent correctness dimensions: inheritance, policy presence, error recovery, determinism, helper handling, and atomic replacement. It is realistically difficult because the defects require repository/history exploration and robust general implementations rather than fixture-specific patches, while the proposed speedrun is substantially longer than the threshold for source-visible tasks. The main weaknesses are underspecified duplicate semantics and failure-injection details, but they do not prevent acceptance if clarified before build.
fixes: Document the exact behavior for duplicate contract names, duplicate aliases, and alias collisions, including which diagnostics and ordering are expected.
Specify a deterministic wirecheck failure-injection mechanism, such as an environment variable, fixture response, or test-only helper mode.
State explicitly whether registry, diagnostics, and summary files must all remain byte-for-byte unchanged after any failed run, and how stale temporary files are handled.
Define the summary schema and ordering rules for all map-like metadata so generated-instance comparisons are unambiguous.
Specify the random seeds, resource limits, and concurrency controls used by generated and interruption tests to avoid flaky verification.

verdicts.reason: This repairs a schema-contract compiler with inheritance and policy resolution, whereas the reference repairs an incident replay and archival database utility.
This concerns compiling versioned contracts into a registry, not classifying and forwarding HTTP routes under a gateway policy.
Although both require deterministic processing and malformed-input handling, the candidate's core problem is contract inheritance and schema compilation rather than binary settlement reconciliation.
The candidate resolves contract schemas and policies, while the reference replays sharded transaction logs into an atomic database snapshot.
The candidate implements inheritance-aware schema compilation, whereas the reference exports authorization audit records using tenant and policy precedence rules.
